checks.a_analysis: I have carefully compared the source document (4 pages) with the JSON output. All paragraph text and list items appear the same number of times in the output as they do in the source. There are no duplicated sections or repeated blocks of text.

The heading hierarchy is correctly flattened into sections, but there is a significant nesting error. The content belonging to the 'CONCLUSIONS OF LAW' section (specifically numbered items 1 through 5 on page 3) is incorrectly nested within the previous 'FINDINGS OF FACT' section's list element. Consequently, the 'CONCLUSIONS OF LAW' section in the JSON (index 6) is missing its primary subordinate content.
checks.b_evidence_source: On page 3, the heading 'CONCLUSIONS OF LAW' is followed by numbered points 1 through 5.
checks.b_evidence_output: The numbered items 1 through 5 (from the Conclusions of Law) are contained within the 'items' array of the second 'list' type element in the 'FINDINGS OF FACT' section (index 5). The 'CONCLUSIONS OF LAW' section (index 6) contains only the transitional sentence 'Based on the foregoing...'.

checks.a_analysis: The document contains a visual box layout on page 1 identifying the parties and the title. The pipeline converted this into a 1x2 table, which correctly preserves the side-by-side structural relationship of the petitioner/respondent vs the document title. No columns are merged or misaligned.

The reading order is materially broken on page 3. The conclusion points (1-5) appear in the JSON sequence before the 'CONCLUSIONS OF LAW' heading that defines them. In the source, the heading precedes the items. In the JSON, the items are part of section 5 ('FINDINGS OF FACT') while the heading is section 6.
checks.b_evidence_source: Source Page 3: Heading 'CONCLUSIONS OF LAW' -> Items 1-5 -> 'Based on the foregoing...' -> Heading 'PROPOSAL FOR DECISION'.
checks.b_evidence_output: Output Reading Order: Section 5 (Items 1-17 Findings AND Items 1-5 Conclusions) -> Section 6 (Heading 'CONCLUSIONS OF LAW' + 'Based on the foregoing...') -> Section 7 (Heading 'PROPOSAL FOR DECISION').

checks.a_analysis: The pipeline failed to distinguish between two distinct numbered lists on page 3. The 'FINDINGS OF FACT' list (1-17) and the 'CONCLUSIONS OF LAW' list (1-5) were merged into a single continuous list structure within Section 5.
checks.b_evidence_source: Page 3 contains two separate numbered lists. One ends at '17. Petitioner has been gainfully employed...' and the next begins at '1. The parties are properly before...'.
checks.b_evidence_output: The second list element in section 5 contains 19 items, merging the end of the findings (items 4-17) with the entirety of the conclusions (items 1-5).

checks.a_analysis: The document contains multiple sections with numbered lists (FINDINGS OF FACT and CONCLUSIONS OF LAW). In the HTML rendering, these lists are affected by a double-numbering defect where the CSS-generated list markers (e.g., '1.', '11.', '15.') are displayed alongside the hardcoded text numbers from the source document (e.g., '1.', '14.', '1.'). Furthermore, the automatic list counter restarts incorrectly after item 3 in 'FINDINGS OF FACT' because an unnumbered paragraph ('A conviction in Vance County...') interrupts the list structure. The counter then continues incorrectly through the next section heading, leading to highly confusing numbering such as '11. 14.' and '15. 1.'. This significantly alters the visual organization and clarity of the numbered points compared to the clean, consistent numbering in the source PDF.
checks.b_evidence_source: Numbered list items in FINDINGS OF FACT (1 through 17) and CONCLUSIONS OF LAW (1 through 5).

checks.b_evidence_location: FINDINGS OF FACT and CONCLUSIONS OF LAW sections, middle to end of document.

The content is clearly readable and aligned.

There are no meaningful images, logos, or charts in the source PDF. The signature line on the final page of the PDF is appropriately represented by a horizontal line character in the HTML. No images are missing or broken.
